name: Chrysalis Apartments
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: The Empowerment Program is replacing its 15-unit former Bainbridge Apartments at 18th and Franklin in Denver's City Park West with Chrysalis Apartments, a seven-story, 70-unit permanent supportive housing building with every home at 30% AMI and backed by state project-based vouchers; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $17M of CHFA bonds and broke ground on 2025-11-19.
why_it_matters: It shows a nonprofit service provider recycling its own aged LIHTC site into deeply targeted PSH by stacking 4% credits and state credits with 70 State Housing Vouchers, a $4.2M Prop 123 PSH grant and a forgivable Denver Homelessness Resolution Fund loan that the city enlarged to cover lost federal 45L credits.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking 2025-11-19); completion not yet reported
status.detail: Pinkard Construction and partners held the groundbreaking on 2025-11-19 with a 14-month build expected, and demolition of the old buildings was complete by January 2026. No financing closing date or completion record was found; completion around early 2027 is inferred from the stated schedule.

next_step: Watch for Denver building inspection and certificate of occupancy records for 1777/1785 Franklin Street and lease-up notices from The Empowerment Program in 2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 30 studios, 35 one-bedroom and 5 two-bedroom units of permanent supportive housing, all with state project-based vouchers.
About $11.4M over 10 years, plus $1,100,000 of state credit.
$6M construction/permanent and $11M construction-only bonds; Denver indicated it would supply volume cap.
0%, 60-year Homelessness Resolution Fund loan ($3.15M approved 2025-04-28, raised by $294,000 on 2025-12-15), with a 60-year covenant.

facts.value: 1777 Franklin Street, Denver 80218 (City Park West), at 18th and Franklin; the December 2025 loan amendment describes the property as 1785 North Franklin Street
N, PSH: new construction, permanent supportive housing
Adults experiencing homelessness with a disabling condition, Empowerment participants and referrals from Denver's Coordinated Assessment System, including people leaving the justice system

Seven stories, about 53,826 sq ft; light-gauge steel BYLD panelized framing over a concrete podium (described as the first BYLD structural system project in the United States); two elevators; all-electric with VTAC units; Zero Energy Ready Homes and Enterprise Green Communities; nine Type A accessible units; 9 parking spaces in the application

The Empowerment Program is lead service provider: behavioral health, trauma and substance-use treatment, HIV/AIDS care, employment and education services, 24/7 peer support front desk; funded by state funds, Medicaid, a services reserve, grants and property cash flow
70 State Housing Vouchers from the Colorado Division of Housing (project-based); the application allowed for vouchers from either the Division of Housing or Denver HOST
Chrysalis Apartments, LLLP, whose general partner is Empowerment Development Corporation II, an affiliate of The Empowerment Program, Inc.
Nonprofit general partner structure intended to qualify for a 100% property tax exemption, per the application
Zoned for the use; concept review completed; seven stories maximizes the density Denver allows for affordable housing, per the application
60-year Denver covenant; CHFA LURA also referenced in the loan agreement

money.note: 2023 Round Two award; the Round Two application requested $1,148,425 and the letter of intent $1,072,000.

CHFA issuer; $6,000,000 construction/permanent and $11,000,000 construction-only, 53.09% of projected aggregate basis; Denver HOST signalled willingness to provide volume cap in a 2023-07-26 letter; private placement or public sale depending on lender, per the application.

background.text: The site held the former Bainbridge Apartments, a 9% LIHTC property past its initial 15-year compliance period, plus an adjacent duplex; together they housed 15 income-restricted units whose residents, all on portable Denver subsidies, were to be relocated to other Empowerment properties.
The project first sought competitive credit: The Empowerment Program applied in 2023 Round One for $1,450,000 of credit and then won federal 4% and state credit in 2023 Round Two.

The application requested a cost basis waiver, citing a 6.8% cost increase since the 2023-02-01 application, about a six-month construction delay, and Davis-Bacon wages estimated at $444,836 ($6,400 per unit).

The market study gave the project its top score in every category except unit size (two-bedroom units slightly small) and projected lease-up of at least 30 units a month; proposed rents were $1,390 (studio), $1,585 (one-bedroom) and $1,925 (two-bedroom), supported by vouchers.

Capitol Hill United Neighborhoods wrote a letter of support on 2023-02-06 after meeting with the team, citing Housing First, trauma-informed design and the decision to build without a natural gas line.

Pinkard's 2024 announcement described a $20 million, 13-month project with groundbreaking anticipated in November 2024; groundbreaking came a year later, and BusinessDen headlined the project as a $36M development.
Denver's December 2025 amendment added a project-based voucher clause: if a HAP contract ends through no fault of the owner, HOST will negotiate in good faith over the affordability terms.

discrepancies.text: The application, CHUN and the sponsor describe the old buildings as holding 15 units, BusinessDen says 20, and Naked Denver describes a 13-unit apartment building plus a duplex.

CHFA and the city give the address as 1777 Franklin Street, 80218, while the application header uses zip 80206, BusinessDen says the demolished buildings were at 1767 and 1777 Franklin, and the city's December 2025 amendment describes the property as 1785 North Franklin Street.
The application plans 9 parking spaces, while Naked Denver reports 8 surface spaces.
CHFA lists 5 two-bedroom units, while the city loan agreement's unit table lists them as a second row of 5 one-bedroom units.
